Bill.BriefDescription: Allowing the director of financial management to include alternative fuel vehicles in a strategy to reduce fuel consumption and emissions from state agency fleets.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to including alternative fuel vehicles in astrategy to reduce fuel consumption and emissions from state agencyfleets; and amending RCW 43.41.130.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 43.41.130 and 2009 c 519 s 6 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The director of financial management, after consultation withother interested or affected state agencies, shall establish overallpolicies governing the acquisition, operation, management, maintenance,repair, and disposal of((,)) all ((passenger)) motor vehicles owned oroperated by any state agency. ((Such)) These policies shall includebut not be limited to a definition of what constitutes authorized useof a state owned or controlled passenger motor vehicle and other motorvehicles on official state business. The definition shall include, butnot be limited to, the use of stateowned motor vehicles for commuterride sharing so long as the entire capital depreciation and operationalexpense of the commuter ridesharing arrangement is paid by thecommuters. Any use other than such defined use shall be considered aspersonal use. p. 1 SHB 3105 (2)(a) By June 15, 2010, the director of the department of generaladministration, in consultation with the office and other interested oraffected state agencies, shall develop strategies to ((reduce)) assiststate agencies in reducing fuel consumption and emissions from allclasses of vehicles. (b) In an effort to achieve lower overall emissions for all classesof vehicles, state agencies should, when financially comparable overthe vehicle's useful life, consider purchasing or converting to ultralow carbon fuel vehicles. (3) State agencies shall ((use these strategies to: (1))) phase in fuel economy standards for motor pools and leasedpetroleumbased fuel vehicles to achieve an average fuel economystandard of thirtysix miles per gallon for passenger vehicle fleets by2015((; (2))). (4) When purchasing light duty passenger vehicles after June 15,2010, state agencies may only purchase: (a) Petroleumbased fuel vehicles that achieve an average fueleconomy of forty miles per gallon ((for light duty passenger vehiclespurchased after June 15, 2010; and (3))); or (b) Ultralow carbon fuel vehicles. (5) When purchasing light duty vans and sport utility vehiclesafter June 15, 2010, state agencies may only purchase: (a) Petroleumbased fuel vehicles that achieve an average fueleconomy standard of twentyseven miles per gallon ((for light duty vansand sport utility vehicles purchased after June 15, 2010)); or (b) Ultralow carbon fuel vehicles. (6) State agencies must report annually on the progress made toachieve the goals under subsections (((1) through)) (3) through (5) ofthis section beginning October 31, 2011. (7) The department of general administration, in consultation withthe office and other affected or interested agencies, shall develop aseparate fleet fuel economy standard for all other classes ofpetroleumbased fuel vehicles and report the progress made towardmeeting the fuel consumption and emissions goals established by thissection to the governor and the relevant legislative committees byDecember 1, 2012. SHB 3105 p. 2 ((For the purposes of this section, light duty vehicles refers tocars, sport utility vehicles, and passenger vans.)) (8) The following vehicles are excluded from the ((agency fleet))average fuel economy ((calculation)) goals established in subsections(3) through (5) of this section: Emergency response vehicles,passenger vans with a gross vehicle weight of eight thousand fivehundred pounds or greater, vehicles that are purchased for offpavementuse, ultralow carbon fuel vehicles, and vehicles that are driven lessthan two thousand miles per year. (9) Average fuel economy calculations used under this section forpetroleumbased fuel vehicles must be based upon the current UnitedStates environmental protection agency composite city and highway mileper gallon rating. (10) The definitions in this subsection apply throughout thissection unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (a) "Petroleumbased fuel vehicle" means a vehicle that uses, as afuel source, more than ten percent gasoline or diesel fuel. (b) "Ultralow carbon fuel vehicle" means a vehicle that uses, asa fuel source, at least ninety percent natural gas, hydrogen,biomethane, or electricity.
